title: Design the core model: paper tooth, pigment deposit, media
description: Decide how paper (tooth height field, fibres), dry media (graphite, coloured pencil, charcoal, pastel, crayon, wax/oil-based) and their deposit, smudging, burnishing and erasing are represented, and how the result is lit. Reuse what fits from oilpaint (spectral Kubelka-Munk mixing, noise, PNG output). Add numba when the first kernel lands.

title: Coloured pencil: little takes over a light first layer
description: A light wash of coloured pencil (two or three layers at pressure 0.3 to 0.5) waxes the tooth so far that darker pencils laid afterwards hardly show: in the first examples/macaw.py, deep green and blue over a lime wash left it lime. A coloured pencil artist builds ten or more light layers, light to dark. Measure how many light layers the model takes before it resists, against that practice, and recalibrate WAX_FULL and RESIST (and what a light touch lays) if it is too few.

title: A full tooth takes hardly any more pastel
description: Once the tooth is full, a further stroke of soft pastel lays next to nothing, and a light stroke over it only catches the grain of the strokes before (shop-window reflections came out as plaid; a red coat over a black car came out striped), unless the layer under it is fixed first. A real soft pastel keeps going on over a full tooth for a while: it is opaque and crumbles on top. The agent drawing examples/broadway.py called fix() every few objects to get round it.

title: No way to rub or erase an area
description: Sheet.smudge and Sheet.erase take one path. Rubbing a sky or a shadow face smooth means writing a sweep of strokes by hand, with a mask as the pressure. Wanted: an area form, as Sheet.shade is for media: an area (rectangle or polygon), a tool, a pressure that may be a function of (x, y), an angle. Note: a tool keeps its load across a stretch of no pressure, so a sweep through a mask carries dust over the gaps; the area form should lift the tool there. Found by the agent drawing examples/deco.py.

title: Strokes laid with the side of a stick stay speckled when rubbed
description: Two layers of sheet.shade(box, charcoal.VINE, 0.8, 9, tilt=1) followed by two finger passes stay speckled (pixel std 0.158 at mean 0.62); the same with the point rubs smooth (std 0.113 at mean 0.66). A finger should even out the side of a stick as it does the point. Found by the agent drawing examples/deco.py, which avoided tilt for that reason.
close_reason: A rubbing tool now spreads the dust under it from grain to grain before it is pressed in (spread_dust, SPREAD, SPREADS in _engine.py); tests in tests/test_dust.py.

title: A firm pencil wears a waxed layer away, stroke by stroke
description: Pressed hard over a waxy layer, a tip drags part of the layer along (burnish). What it still carried when the stroke ended left the paper with it, so many short firm strokes wore the layer away. Found drawing examples/macaw.py. Fix: lay what the tip drags on the marked paper under it where it lifts off (set_down in _engine.py); only off the sheet is it lost.
close_reason: What a polishing tip drags is laid where it lifts off, and it is laid back within a pixel or two (BURNISH_LAY 4), so a firm pencil no longer wears a waxed layer away nor leaves blobs where its strokes end.

title: A shading helper: fill an area with strokes as a hand does
description: Shading only looks like pencil when the strokes do what a hand does: side by side at an angle, none quite straight or alike, lighter where the pencil lands and lifts. examples/pencils.py has such a function (shade); make it part of the library, with cross-hatching by shading again at another angle.
close_reason: Sheet.shade, with tests; examples/pencils.py uses it

title: Colour: coloured pencil and pastel, layering, wax, burnishing

notes: Revisit sanded card's tooth when pastel comes: with a pencil it covers only 57% of the sheet after many firm layers, because its tooth is mostly low with pointed peaks. Real sanded card takes pigment evenly.
close_reason: Coloured pencils and pastels, two layers of dust for order, wax resist and burnishing; tests for behaviours 4 and 5

title: Tips: wear, tilt, the side of a stick, crayon; graphite shine
description: Step 5 of docs/design.md.
notes: Built: tilt (round points), wear (Stick, a tip whose flat grows with the volume laid; sharpen), crayon and oil pastel (crayons.wax, pastels.oil) with resist depending on what is laid over wax (resist_of), and graphite's shine (Medium.sheen, Sheet.shine, render(gloss=...)). Known limits: the side of a stick is the same 5 times its width for every medium (SIDE), which may be too narrow for a long stick of charcoal. A held medium laid over dust (coloured pencil over pastel) ends up under it. A kneaded eraser lifts the unheld share of an oil pastel like dust, which a real one would not. Charcoal over a single firm crayon line still greys it, since one line's film is not yet as slick as it gets (WAX_FULL). Only graphite has sheen: polished wax (burnished coloured pencil, crayon) does not shine yet. A tip pressed hard does not flatten the paper's tooth, so shine still glints on the grain.
close_reason: Tilt, wear, crayon, oil pastel and graphite's shine are built; the limits left are in the notes.

title: A stroke has one width and round ends
description: A stroke keeps one width from end to end, and its ends are always round. Wanted: a width that can vary along the stroke (a profile, as pressure has), for strokes that recede in perspective or taper; and flat ends for the side or the end of a stick (car bodies, awnings, the bars of a crossing had to be inset by half a width). Found by the agent drawing examples/broadway.py.

title: Light strokes leave streaks that rubbing does not close
description: A light stroke marks narrower than its width (the rim of the tip hardly touches). Vine charcoal at width 7, 4.2 px apart, pressure 0.4, left white streaks between strokes, and a finger or chamois did not close them: rubbing should spread the dust over the bare paper between. Found by the agent drawing examples/deco.py.
close_reason: A rubbing tool now spreads the dust under it from grain to grain before it is pressed in (spread_dust, SPREAD, SPREADS in _engine.py); tests in tests/test_dust.py.

title: A stump hardly smooths compressed charcoal
description: Compressed charcoal (binding 0.45) stays as laid under a stump, so smooth darks had to be vine underneath with compressed on top. A stump does blend compressed charcoal in life, less easily than vine. Check what share of it a stump moves, against vine, and decide. Found by the agent drawing examples/deco.py.
close_reason: A rubbing tool now spreads the dust under it from grain to grain before it is pressed in (spread_dust, SPREAD, SPREADS in _engine.py); tests in tests/test_dust.py.

title: Ballpoint: blobs of ink and the sheen of heavy ink
description: Two things a real ballpoint does that fusain.pens does not: the ball gathers ink and leaves a blob where a line starts or turns sharply; and heavy layers of ink have a bronze sheen under a lamp (the ink layer carries no sheen, and Sheet.shine looks only at the held layer). The groove the ball presses into the paper is fusain-dyh.

title: A firm tip does not flatten or indent the paper
description: press is raised only by burnishing wax, and it means level with the peaks of the tooth. A firm pencil does not flatten the tooth (so graphite's shine still glints on the grain), and there is no way to indent a line below the surface, as a stylus or a ballpoint does, for a pencil shaded over it to skip. Needs a depth-below-surface field, separate from press.

title: Polished wax does not shine
description: Only graphite has sheen. A burnished coloured pencil or a heavy crayon has a waxy gloss under a lamp. Give wax a sheen that grows with press, and check that the colour examples stay believable.

title: A kneaded eraser lifts oil pastel like dust
description: The share of an oil pastel that the paper does not hold at once lies in the dust layers, so a kneaded eraser lifts it as it lifts charcoal. A real oil pastel smears under a finger but does not come off on a kneaded eraser; it has to be scraped.

title: Charcoal over one firm crayon line still greys it
description: A single firm line of wax crayon lays a film of wax thinner than WAX_FULL, so it is not yet as slick as it gets, and it is pressed level, so charcoal dust lies over all of it: charcoal shaded over the line leaves it as dark as the grainy paper around it. Wax resist with dry media therefore does not show for single lines (it does over three firm layers: tests/test_crayons.py).

title: The side of a stick is as wide for every medium
description: A stick held on its side marks a band five times the width of its point (SIDE in _engine.py), whatever it is. That suits a pencil lead; a long stick of charcoal or pastel laid flat marks a band as wide as the stick is long. Let the medium or the Stick say how long its side is.

title: A held medium laid over dust ends up under it
description: The held layer is always rendered under the two dust layers. A coloured pencil or a crayon drawn over pastel or charcoal dust therefore shows under the dust, where in life it lies over it and partly binds it.

title: Make strokes faster
description: Shading 1120x820 pixels with an HB of width 6 takes about 2.4 s (2.1 s before colour was added). The time is in lay_stroke's work per pixel under the tip: each pixel is visited by about nine steps of the tip, and each visit hashes three numbers, takes a power and a square root, and loops over the 24 bands. Ideas: a table of the streaks per pass, the jitter once per pixel, fewer steps for wide tips. The drawing must stay byte-identical (tools: a fingerprint of held, under, loose, cover and press).

title: Calibrate graphite tones against scans of real pencil
description: The constants of fusain/_engine.py were set so that tones land near figures estimated from experience (docs/design.md, One step of a stroke), not measured. Scan swatches of real 4H, HB, 2B and 6B on cartridge paper at a few pressures and numbers of layers, and fit the constants to them.

title: Extras: fixative, hatching helpers, ballpoint pen
description: Step 6 of docs/design.md. Ballpoint needs its own deposit rule: a paste laid at a steady rate.
notes:
Fixative built (Sheet.fix, Sheet.fixed). Hatching helpers: Sheet.shade covers them (angle, spacing, hand). Left: the ballpoint pen. It cannot indent the paper until fusain-dyh gives a depth below the surface.
Ballpoint pen built (fusain.pens, Sheet.ink): its own kernel (roll_stroke) and its own layer, a stain under everything else. Not built: the groove it presses into the paper (fusain-dyh), the blob of ink where a line starts or turns, the sheen of heavy ink.
close_reason: Fixative, hatching (Sheet.shade) and the ballpoint pen are built; what is left of the pen is in the notes and in fusain-dyh.
